literature_type_guess: sanctification call (single-verse directive)
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל הָעָ֖ם הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ is a full messenger formula marking a change of speaker, not a change of addressee: the officers who commanded הָעָם in 3:3 (וַיְצַוּוּ֮ אֶת הָעָ֣ם) give way to Joshua speaking in his own voice at 3:5, while the addressee, הָעָם, stays constant across the 3:4|5 seam. That speaker-change-plus-fresh-formula is the near-edge driver. The far edge is where the addressee genuinely does change: 3:6 turns from הָעָם to הַכֹּהֲנִים, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֔ר.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Describing the evidence as 'thin, marker-only' and capping confidence at medium_low was this draft's original position; it misclassified the evidence. A later revision misdescribed the near edge as an addressee change from officers to people, but 3:3's officers already address הָעָם, so the addressee does not shift there - the real near-edge signal is the speaker change from officers to Joshua. Absorbing this verse into the following priestly command (v.6) as a single 'Joshua's instructions' block remains a live alternative, since both are Joshua speaking on the same day, but the different addressees (people vs. priests) keep 3:5 and 3:6 apart on the same driving-signal basis this draft uses throughout ch.3.

literature_type_guess: summons formula: call to attention before Joshua's proclamation
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גֹּ֣שׁוּ הֵ֔נָּה וְשִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶֽם opens a fresh messenger formula with the addressee shifted to the whole nation (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), distinct from vv.7-8's Joshua-alone address to the priests. Its content is a bare summons to attention rather than the promise itself; the actual content commences at 3:10 with its own explicit-subject reset, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ, naming Joshua again rather than continuing null-subject. That renewed named subject is the same class of signal this cluster already treats as boundary-forming at 3:5, 3:6 and 3:7 (short units opened by a repeated, explicitly named אמר-formula), so consistency favors reading 3:9 as its own brief unit rather than folding it into 3:10-13's proclamation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 3:9-13 as one unbroken proclamation, on the ground that both verses share the same speaker and addressee and the summons naturally introduces what follows, was this draft's original position. It is abandoned because the original rationale claimed no new אמר-formula interrupts the span, and 3:10's וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ contradicts that claim directly - it is a full, explicit-subject reset, not a null-subject continuation like 4:21's (see M8-Josh-022), so the campaign's own explicit-subject-reset principle argues for the split rather than against it.

literature_type_guess: divine word and place-name etiology: the reproach of Egypt and the naming of Gilgal
boundary_rationale: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ הַיּ֗וֹם גַּלּ֛וֹתִי אֶת חֶרְפַּ֥ת מִצְרַ֖יִם מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֑ם opens a fresh, complete messenger formula (unit-opening at 3:7/4:1/4:15/6:2/7:10) and closes on its own naming-etiology, וַיִּקְרָ֞א שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ גִּלְגָּ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה, the 'to this day' class decisive at 6:25/7:26/8:29. Both edges are independently formula-evidenced despite the unit being one verse. The forward pull toward 5:10-12 is real and is engaged rather than dismissed: 5:9 itself supplies the place name Gilgal that 5:10 immediately repeats, וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּגִּלְגָּ֑ל, and 5:10 opens with two ordinary wayyiqtol clauses - encamping, then keeping the Passover - not a 'date-formula'; the fourteenth-of-the-month date sits mid-verse, inside the Passover clause, not at its head. That catchword link is a genuine bridge between adjacent units, but it does not override the formal seam: 5:9 is Yahweh's quoted speech, sealed by its own decisive etiological closure, while 5:10 is narrated report with the nation, not Yahweh, as grammatical subject, opening an unrelated topic with no quotation formula of any kind. The closure-type and the speech-to-narration shift are what actually separate the two verses; the shared place name is a link between neighbouring units, not evidence that they are one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v.9 into 5:2-8 as its capstone, the previous position, does not survive the formula test applied elsewhere. Attaching v.9 forward to Passover (5:10-12) is the more serious alternative, and it was previously dismissed on a false description of 5:10 as opening 'its own date-formula with no connecting particle and unrelated content' - 5:10 in fact opens on two plain wayyiqtol verbs and its date phrase falls mid-verse, and its very first action-clause names Gilgal again, the place 5:9 has just named. That catchword is acknowledged rather than argued away; the merge is still not adopted, because 5:9 remains Yahweh's own quoted word sealed by a discrete 'to this day' etiology, while 5:10 is third-person narration of the nation's own action opening a new topic (Passover) with no speech formula - a stronger pair of differentiators than the mark-based or formula-shape claims previously offered.

literature_type_guess: divine battle-plan speech, with its circumstantial premise (Jericho shut up) and the seven-day circuit tactics
boundary_rationale: The unit now opens with its circumstantial frame, וִֽירִיחוֹ֙ סֹגֶ֣רֶת וּמְסֻגֶּ֔רֶת מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל - a disjunctive background clause that fronts its subject (וִירִיחוֹ) before a double participial predicate (סֹגֶרֶת וּמְסֻגֶּרֶת, 'shut up and barred'), with no wayyiqtol anywhere in the verse - which the following divine word directly answers: רְאֵה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי בְיָֽדְךָ֔ אֶת יְרִיח֖וֹ. From v.2, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ opens the full tactical plan - six days of single circuits, a seventh day of sevenfold circuits, trumpets, the shout - as one continuous divine speech, closed before Joshua's relay-command begins in v.6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating v.1 as its own separate decision was original; abandoned because 6:1's fronted-subject-plus-participle clause carries no wayyiqtol and functions as pure scene-setting background, directly answered by v.2's own wayyiqtol. Citing 2:6 and 4:9 as parallels of the same verbless shape was the earlier ground for that reading; both are withdrawn as parallels, since 2:6 (וְהִ֖יא הֶעֱלָ֣תַם הַגָּ֑גָה) and 4:9 (וּשְׁתֵּ֧ים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֲבָנִ֗ים הֵקִ֣ים) are each a finite qatal clause, not verbless at all - and 4:9 carries its own 'to this day' closure and forms its own unit (M8-Josh-152), the opposite of background material. The merge does not depend on either parallel: 6:1's own syntax - fronted subject, double participle, no finite narrative verb - is what marks it as background answered by v.2's wayyiqtol. Splitting vv.3-4 from v.5 was also considered, but both remain inside the same uninterrupted quotation with no new formula between them.

literature_type_guess: destruction of Ai and the king's execution
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֣י כְּכַלּ֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל לַהֲרֹג֩ shifts to the mopping-up and total-count report, the king's hanging and cairn, closing with a second 'to this day' notice, גַּל אֲבָנִ֣ים גָּד֔וֹל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה, mirroring 7:26's Achan cairn. This וַיְהִי כְּכַלּוֹת clause is boundary-forming here on positional grounds: it stands at the head of a fresh report - the total count of the fallen (v.25), the burning of the city, and the king's execution and cairn (vv.26-29) all follow as content the preceding decision (M8-Josh-047, closing at 8:23 with the king taken alive) does not reach. The same construction recurs at 10:20 inside M8-Josh-059 without opening a unit there, because it sits inside a pursuit already underway since 10:19's command and closes off action already in progress rather than heading a fresh report; the two instances are resolved by that positional principle, not by any claim about which side's killing had or had not already been narrated.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this into the Ebal altar-building of vv.30-35 as one 'aftermath of Ai' unit was considered, but v.30's אָ֣ז marks a fresh, undated jump away from Ai entirely, treated as its own scene by the next decision. An earlier version of the reconciliation with M8-Josh-059 claimed the field-slaughter of Ai's other inhabitants 'is new' at this verse; that is inaccurate - 8:21-22, inside the immediately preceding M8-Josh-047 span, already narrate the field-slaughter twice (וַיָּשֻׁ֕בוּ וַיַּכּ֖וּ אֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעָֽי; וַיַּכּ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִ֥יר) before this verse's completion clause restates it. The positional principle above - fresh report versus already-open pursuit - replaces that narrated/unnarrated test.

literature_type_guess: Ebal altar-building, law inscription, and covenant reading
boundary_rationale: אָ֣ז יִבְנֶ֤ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ opens with the אָז+yiqtol construction this book uses to jump scenes, matching 10:12 (אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֤ר) and 22:1 (אָ֚ז יִקְרָ֣א), a real comparative pattern against 10:33's אָז+qatal (אָ֣ז עָלָ֗ה), left unit-internal by this draft. That signal is secondary - established only by comparison across three other passages - but genuine, and co-occurs with a total location change to Mount Ebal. boundary_rationale: וַיָּ֤שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ marks a return-to-base notice (v.15) immediately undercut by the discovery report about the hiding kings and Joshua's command to seal the cave and continue pursuit (vv.16-19), closing with the army's peaceful return to Makkedah (v.21). The two instances are distinguished by their position relative to the surrounding report, not by which side had already narrated its killing: 8:24 stands at the head of a fresh report - the total count, the city's burning, and the king's execution and cairn all follow it as new content - while 10:20 sits inside a pursuit already opened at v.19's imperative, רִדְפוּ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֹֽיְבֵיכֶ֔ם, with the same participants (Joshua and the sons of Israel) carried forward without a subject reset, and no closure tag anywhere between v.19 and v.21's own return-to-camp notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 10:15-19/10:20-21 by bare analogy to 8:24 was considered and rejected on the position-based principle above. An earlier version of this reconciliation tested whether each construction's content had already been narrated, stating that 8:24 was boundary-forming because 'the field-slaughter is not yet narrated' there, against 10:20 merely 'closing off action already commanded.' That test in fact ran backward: 8:21-22 (וַיָּשֻׁ֕בוּ וַיַּכּ֖וּ אֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעָֽי; וַיַּכּ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִ֥יר) narrate the field-slaughter twice before 8:24's completion clause, while 10:19 only commands the pursuit and nothing narrates its execution before 10:20 declares it complete - the opposite of what the test assumed. That narrated/unnarrated test is dropped here in favor of the position-based one above: 10:20 stays inside this span because it closes off pursuit already commanded within it, with unbroken participant continuity and no intervening closure tag, not because of any claim about what had or had not been told.

Disclosed at the near edge: v.8 opens on the bound form עִמּ֗וֹ, whose antecedent, וַחֲצִ֖י הַשֵּׁ֥בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּֽׁה, sits at the end of v.7 - the unit's first word cannot be parsed without reaching back across the seam. Weighed against this: the discourse-mode shift from second-person imperative ('divide this land,' v.7) to third-person narration ('the Reubenites and Gadites have taken,' v.8) is judged the more decisive signal, marking the transition from quoted command to narratorial exposition. A caveat on the comparison drawn to 3:14: that verse is not a clean 'boundary without a formula' precedent, since 3:14 itself opens on its own וַיְהִי-plus-infinitive-construct device (וַיְהִ֗י בִּנְסֹ֤עַ הָעָם֙ מֵאָ֣הֳלֵיהֶ֔ם), the same construction credited as unit-opening at M8-Josh-023; 13:8, by contrast, has no opener of its own at all, only the bound עִמּוֹ reaching back into v.7. The discourse-mode shift therefore has to carry this seam on its own merits, without a formula-free precedent to lean on; the resumptive עִמּוֹ is read as the narrator's own linking device into that exposition, not proof vv.7-8 form one unbroken unit. Confidence is lowered to reflect this unresolved backward dependency.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Leaving the עִמּוֹ dependency unaddressed, as originally drafted, is not defensible. Re-cutting to include v.7's second half inside this unit was considered to resolve the dependency structurally; not adopted because it would split a single grammatical sentence (Yahweh's one command, running to v.7's end) mid-verse, which this campaign avoids absent much stronger reason, and the discourse-mode boundary genuinely falls at the verse seam even though the pronoun reaches back across it.

literature_type_guess: tribal boundary description: Judah's south border
boundary_rationale: וַיְהִ֣י הַגּוֹרָ֗ל לְמַטֵּ֛ה בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה opens a fresh lot-formula distinct from the Moses-grant formula used for the Transjordan tribes, marking the start of Cisjordan's lot-cast allotments, and this first segment traces only the southern border, closing with its own deictic sub-colophon, זֶה יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֥וּל נֶֽגֶב. This is the same closural class - a deictic demonstrative (זֶה/זֹאת) plus a border-region noun - now confirmed to recur at Josh.18.14 (זֹ֖את פְּאַת יָֽם) and Josh.18.19 (זֶ֖ה גְּב֥וּל נֶֽגֶב), where M8-Josh-111 originally, and wrongly, denied that any such internal closing tag existed in Benjamin's border description. With that error corrected and Benjamin's border split accordingly (M8-Josh-111/160/161), the device is attested three times across two tribes rather than once, which strengthens rather than weakens the case for reading it as decisive wherever it appears. Both controls point the same direction without depending on each other. Disclosed, non-boundary: a samekh is attested after Josh.21.37, but that site falls inside this span (before v.38), not at either edge, and is recorded here as an interior marker rather than filed as boundary evidence. Medium_low reflects that the heading-to-tally shape survives either textual reading of vv.36-37, while the closing number itself remains textually unstable - the discount properly reflects that the closing arithmetic, not the boundary location, is what the variance touches.

boundary_rationale: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ וַיֵּלְכ֡וּ shifts subject to the departing tribes' journey and their altar-building at the Jordan, then to the western tribes' alarmed response and muster at Shiloh 'to go up against them to war' - a rising-conflict unit distinct from the preceding farewell scene and from the confrontation speech that follows. strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this through the delegation's arrival and opening accusation (vv.13-20) as one 'conflict escalates' unit was considered, but v.13 introduces named individuals (Phinehas, and per v.14 the ten tribal chiefs) and a formal embassy, a distinct diplomatic episode from the general mustering just narrated. literature_type_guess: assembly notice and Joshua's self-introduction
boundary_rationale: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִיָּמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים אַ֠חֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר הֵנִ֨יחַ יְהוָ֧ה marks a large, undated time-jump ('after many days') and a new occasion - Joshua's old age now motivating a farewell assembly - naming the summoned leadership classes. v.2 closes with Joshua's own brief self-introduction in direct speech, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אֲנִ֣י זָקַ֔נְתִּי בָּ֖אתִי בַּיָּמִֽים ('I am old, well advanced in years'); this is not quotation-free narration, as previously stated. What distinguishes vv.1-2 from v.3 is not the presence or absence of a speech verb but content: vv.1-2 cover the temporal frame, the summons, and Joshua's own age-based self-introduction, while the substantive retrospective-and-charge address - what Yahweh has done, what Israel must do - opens only at v.3's וְאַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֗ם. The span is unchanged; only the stated ground is corrected.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this notice into Joshua's speech that follows (making 23:1-8 one unit) was considered, since v.2's self-introduction and v.3's substantive address are both direct speech with no formula break between them; it remains split here because the content shifts from Joshua introducing himself by age to Joshua reciting Yahweh's deeds and charging the nation, a real content pivot even though both sides of it are technically quoted speech.

literature_type_guess: Joshua's exhortation to fidelity: retrospective and positive charge
boundary_rationale: וְאַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֗ם is not the opening of Joshua's address - that opened one verse earlier at 23:2b with his self-introduction - but an intra-speech pivot marked by the fronted second-person pronoun וְאַתֶּם, turning from the speaker's own age and self-introduction to the addressees' witnessed experience of what Yahweh has done. The unit runs from that pivot through the charge to hold fast and not turn aside, to a concluding appeal, לְאַהֲבָ֖ה אֶת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם, before the discourse pivots again to a negative conditional scenario at v.12 marked by כִּ֣י אִם. A consonantal sweep of the whole book confirms רק/וְרַק occurs fifteen times in Joshua - 1:7, 1:17, 1:18, 6:15, 6:17, 6:18 (וְרַק), 6:24, 8:2, 8:27, 11:13, 11:14, 11:22, 13:6, 13:14 and 22:5 - and not once inside chapter 23. v.6 opens וַחֲזַקְתֶּ֣ם מְאֹ֔ד with no comparable particle at all. With that phantom removed, v.6 supplies no independent competing signal of its own kind, and the whole positive exhortation from the v.3 pivot through v.11 is kept as one sustained unit on that corrected basis.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v.6's וַחֲזַקְתֶּ֣ם מְאֹ֔ד ('be very strong') as a rhetorical pivot within the speech was considered, mirroring how ch.1 is segmented at רַק חֲזַק וֶאֱמַץ מְאֹד (1:7); it loses because v.6 continues the same positive charge begun at the v.3 pivot without introducing a new topic the way v.12's conditional genuinely does. An earlier version of this row's fix over-corrected in stating that רק occurs only twice in the whole book, at 1:7 and 22:5; a full consonantal scan finds fifteen occurrences across chs.1, 6, 8, 11, 13 and 22 (never in ch.23), so the whole-book count is struck as false while the verse-local claim it was meant to support - that no רק exists anywhere in ch.23 to test against 1:7 - is independently true and is all the argument actually requires.

It echoes 21:45's colophon in substance - 21:45 reads לֹֽא נָפַ֣ל דָּבָ֔ר מִכֹּל֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַטּ֔וֹב אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה - and 23:14 restates the claim twice in its own wording, לֹֽא נָפַל֩ דָּבָ֨ר אֶחָ֜ד מִכֹּ֣ל הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הַטּוֹבִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם and again לֹֽא נָפַ֥ל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ דָּבָ֥ר אֶחָֽד, now applying the formula symmetrically to future curse as well as past blessing. literature_type_guess: covenant-lawsuit historical prologue (Yahweh's recital through Joshua)
boundary_rationale: כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ opens a single sustained first-person divine recital - the patriarchs, the Egyptian plagues, the Reed Sea, the Transjordan conquest, Balaam, the Jordan crossing, and the hornet driving out the kings - running as one unbroken speech with no reintroduction of the messenger formula between its historical movements. Both primary reviewers independently searched the full running Hebrew of vv.3-13 for any reintroduced כֹּה אָמַר / וַיֹּאמֶר / לֵאמֹר and found none; the unbroken first-person chain runs from וָ֠אֶקַּח at v.3 to וָאֶתֵּ֨ן לָכֶ֜ם at v.13.
